# Pitex 2.2.1

This patch improves embedded live-compile reliability and TeX compatibility.

## Changes

- Add `\partokencontext` and `\partokenname` support for current LaTeX and `microtype`. Valid documents no longer show undefined-control-sequence errors for these commands.
- Restart an interrupted preview worker even when it has not created its first checkpoint. Later edits can start a new compile.
- Correct Unicode math and delimiter primitive offsets. `unicode-math` documents compile without stray delimiter codes in the page.
- Preserve shaped source text as PDF `ActualText`. Ligatures retain their original characters for copy and search.
- Map OpenType math script variants to their base Unicode characters. Superscripts and subscripts remain available when copying preview text.
- Rebuild the embedded format cache under a versioned cache key.
- Rewrite the application README using ASD-STE100 Issue 9 writing rules. Correct its Markdown-preview availability description.

## Validation

- Compare 27 TeX fixtures with installed XeLaTeX, including math, native fonts, Korean, tables, graphics, TikZ/PGFPlots, chemistry, circuits, imports, and existing bibliography data. Exercise two unsaved generations per fixture.
- Check repeated and rapid edits, real TeX error reporting and recovery, and interruption before the first checkpoint.
- Run the macOS application integration checks for save behavior, preview publication, manual-build priority, SyncTeX, export, backend cleanup, and late native-font loading.
- Run parser regressions with AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer, and verify source provenance and helper linkage.

These local runtime checks used a full Xcode installation and TeX Live 2026 on Apple Silicon. Linux and Windows validation uses hosted CI. macOS 15 runtime behavior remains unverified.

## Downloads and limits

This release supplies a macOS ARM64 DMG and Ubuntu 24.04/22.04 AMD64 packages. Windows beta downloads remain on hold.

The embedded preview uses XeTeX. Documents that require pdfTeX/LuaTeX commands or shell execution need the compiler backend. New bibliography data still requires BibTeX or Biber in the project build workflow. PostScript specials and PDF navigation annotations remain outside the embedded preview's supported output.
